title: Flight Deck: Cohort Release Windows and Signal-Based Model Deprioritization Matrix
creator: Ravi Menon
project: Hosted API Roadmap - Q2 Cohort Runway
description: Establish a repeatable quarterly cadence for cohort-based release windows across the Hosted API model catalog. Deliver a signal-driven matrix that automatically deprioritizes models from high-traffic cohorts when quality or infra signals cross thresholds, enabling predictable capacity hedging and reduced firefighting during seasonal ramps. This ticket scopes the PM work: definition of cohort buckets, signal taxonomy (quality/latency/cost), deprioritization rules, cross-functional rollout calendar, and handoffs to engineering for automation and dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Cohort taxonomy defined and documented (3 primary cohorts + experiment lane + reserve lane).
Signal taxonomy published (model-quality, p50/p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens, error-rate, KV cache hit-rate).
Deprioritization matrix with thresholds and fallback model mappings approved by Eng and SRE.
Runway calendar with release windows for Q2 published to stakeholders and linked in the roadmap.
Implementation plan (handoff) with clear owner for automation tasks (autoscaler rules, routing policies).
Dashboard prototype linkable from Console showing cohort health and active deprioritization events.
notes: Trade-offs: conservative deprioritization favors user continuity (soft-deprioritization first) vs. aggressive capacity protection (hard cuts); propose two-step policy.
We should default experiment lane to 10% of cohort capacity with nightly sweeps; reserve lane for sudden spikes.
Consider exposing cohort opt-outs for enterprise customers on Dedicated/Dedicated-like contracts.
decisions: Use cohort buckets by traffic signature (seeded by customer cohort and traffic profile) instead of ad-hoc hostnames.
Two-step deprioritization: (1) soft: reduce model weight and enable cache-prefers, (2) hard: route to fallback model variant.
Require Eng to support a model-compatibility manifest for fallback mapping (minimum latency/quality contract).
stakeholders: Serving Runtime Eng Lead: Marcus Chen
risks: False positives in signals could reduce perceived quality for paying customers — need canary staging and rollback windows.
Model fallback compatibility: some models produce degraded semantics when swapped; must build eval guardrails.
Operational complexity: additional routing and autoscaler rules increase triage surface for SRE.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Design): Mar 10 - Mar 24: finalize taxonomy, thresholds, and matrix (PM + Eng review).
Phase 1 (Pilot): Apr 1 - Apr 15: run cohort pilot on 2 non-critical cohorts with read-only deprioritization metrics enabled.
Phase 2 (Automate): Apr 16 - Apr 30: implement autoscaler hooks and routing fallback mapping; add dashboard alerts.
Phase 3 (Q2 Launch): May 1: open deployment for opt-in cohorts; evaluate and iterate via weekly retros.
metrics: Operational: number of deprioritization events per week, mean time to revert a deprioritization action.
Performance: p50/p95 latency delta and tail-error-rate for affected cohorts.
Cost: tokens/sec cost delta and estimated monthly savings from saved capacity during spikes.
Quality: percent of responses flagged as regression vs baseline evals for swapped models.
